definition: Questions about the direction something is facing or moving, such as the direction the dog or duck is facing, or the orientation of the school bus.
Questions that focus on the existence or non-existence of certain elements or features in the image.
Questions that pertain to the state or condition of an object, such as whether a flag is blowing in the wind or if the ground is wet.
Questions about the number of objects or features present in the image.
This aspect refers to the model's ability to understand the position and relationship of objects or elements within an image in relation to each other and their surroundings.
Questions regarding the color of certain objects or elements.
This category involves the model's ability to identify and analyze the physical attributes and structural features of objects in an image.
Questions related to text or symbols present in the image.
Questions concerning the perspective from which the photo was taken.
Questions that fit none of the nine visual patterns: identifying or naming what is in the image, or recalling knowledge about it, with no visual property named.
